references.name: Faces
references.summary: Select named planar faces for within-component feature operations.
references.use_when: Pass a Faces value to operations such as Shape.on() and Shape.shell() to identify a surface of the target body.
references.limits: The enum defines all six cardinal faces. Individual operations may support only a subset; Shape.on() currently accepts TOP and BOTTOM. Component assembly attachment uses Anchor instead.

references.name: Anchor
references.summary: Select component attachment references and cardinal directions.
references.use_when: Use cardinal or corner anchors to attach reusable component occurrences, or combine cardinal values to identify Box edges/corners.
references.limits: Anchor is the assembly/alignment vocabulary. Within-component feature placement normally uses Faces instead. INNER_BOTTOM has no direction vector and therefore cannot be used as a cardinal selector.

references.name: Axis
references.summary: Select one of the native principal X, Y or Z axes.
references.use_when: Use Axis for primitive orientation and supported patterns, for example Cylinder(..., axis=Axis.X) or a linear Hole pattern along Axis.Y.
references.limits: Axis is a principal-axis selector, not an attachment reference and not an extrusion Direction.

references.name: Depth
references.summary: Choose a supported feature-depth policy.
references.use_when: Use Depth.THROUGH_ALL for features such as Hole that should pass completely through their target instead of using a fixed distance.
references.limits: THROUGH_ALL is currently the only named depth policy.

references.name: Edges
references.summary: Select edges for supported fillet and chamfer feature operations.
references.use_when: Use Edges.VERTICAL for the vertical edges of a supported rectangular body. Use from_profile() for named profile segments and from_vertices() for extrusion-axis edges grown from named profile vertices.
references.limits: Only the selectors implemented here are public. from_profile() currently supports sides="both"; from_vertices() requires named Polygon2D vertices.

references.name: Shape
references.summary: Store Forge geometry and feature operations before SolidCraft executes them.
references.use_when: Shape values are normally returned by constructors such as Box(), Cylinder(), Hole() and Sketch.extrude(), then transformed or combined with the supported Shape methods/operators.
references.limits: Shape is only Forge's description of the model. SolidCraft owns the final BRep and feature history; users normally do not instantiate Shape(kind, data) directly.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Forge node type. Public constructors set this; normal model code should not invent kind values.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Data stored for that node type. Public constructors and methods build this payload.

references.name: component
references.summary: Declare one reusable physical component definition.
references.use_when: Decorate a model class whose build() result represents one reusable physical part. Child defaults stay fixed unless explicitly published with include=. Parent Parameter/Expression inputs remain symbolic.
references.limits: build() must produce one Shape when reused as a component.

parameters.name: cls
parameters.description: Model class whose build() returns one physical part. Omit when using @component(...) as a decorator factory.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Child default parameters to publish. Use names, "*", or a mapping for renamed shared parameters.

references.name: assembly
references.summary: Declare a reusable class that composes component occurrences.
references.use_when: Decorate a class when the class itself represents a reusable assembly or subassembly built from component occurrences and their relationships.
references.limits: build() must return a component occurrence or Assembly. The decorator does not itself create grouping or attachment relationships; those come from the objects returned by build().

parameters.name: cls
parameters.description: Model class whose build() returns a component occurrence or Assembly.

references.name: Occurrence.copy
references.summary: Create another occurrence of the same reusable definition.
references.use_when: Reuse one component definition for another physical occurrence.
references.limits: Attachment state is occurrence-specific and is not copied.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Optional explicit Forge name for the new occurrence.

parameters.name: placement
parameters.description: Optional absolute Placement for the new occurrence. When omitted, the source placement is inherited.

references.name: Occurrence.attach
references.summary: Create a rigid or planar relationship from this occurrence to another component.
references.use_when: Placement should be expressed semantically between component references, such as left face to right face or one mounting frame to another, rather than as a calculated global XYZ position.
references.limits: The target must be another component occurrence. Supported standard anchors currently focus on rectangular component geometry; custom AnchorFrame/AnchorTopology references cover more specific datums. as_built=True requires all other relationship arguments to remain at their defaults.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Parent component occurrence to attach to.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Attachment reference on target. Defaults to Anchor.RIGHT.

parameters.name: child
parameters.description: Attachment reference on this occurrence. Defaults to Anchor.LEFT.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: In-plane (u, v) offset on the parent attachment plane, in mm. Defaults to (0, 0).

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Separation along the parent anchor normal, in mm. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Optional joint rotation in degrees.

parameters.name: as_built
parameters.description: When True, keep the occurrences at their existing poses and create an as-built rigid joint.

references.signature: Occurrence.attach(self, target, *, parent=<Anchor.RIGHT: 'right'>, child=<Anchor.LEFT: 'left'>, offset=(0, 0), gap=0, angle=None, as_built=False)

references.name: Occurrence.group
references.summary: Place this occurrence in a named native subassembly component.
references.use_when: Give one occurrence a useful native browser/subassembly parent.
references.limits: Grouping changes hierarchy only. It does not align, attach or otherwise create a mechanical relationship. One occurrence cannot belong to several different groups.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Native group/subassembly name.

references.name: Assembly.group
references.summary: Wrap these assembly occurrences in a real nested native component.
references.use_when: The collection should appear as one named subassembly/browser unit in SolidCraft.
references.limits: Grouping changes native hierarchy, not placement or relationships. Use attach() for mechanical relationships between occurrences.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Native subassembly/browser component name.

references.name: Assembly.with_anchor
references.summary: Expose one named attachment datum owned by this assembly.
references.use_when: A mounting/reference name belongs to the meaning of the larger assembly rather than to the generic reusable component itself.
references.limits: target must already belong to this Assembly. with_anchor() exposes a reference; it does not create an attachment by itself.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Public name for the assembly-owned attachment datum.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Component occurrence in this Assembly that owns the real attachment reference.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Anchor, named component anchor, AnchorFrame or AnchorTopology on target.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Optional in-plane (u, v) correction passed through when attaching, in mm.

references.name: Assembly.anchor
references.summary: Return one named assembly-owned attachment datum.
references.use_when: A consumer needs the target/reference pair previously exposed with with_anchor() in order to create an attachment.
references.limits: The name must resolve to exactly one assembly-owned anchor.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name previously registered with with_anchor().

references.name: Shape.at
references.summary: Place a shape at absolute coordinates or align it to another Shape.
references.use_when: Use shape.at(x, y, z) for geometric placement. Box, Cylinder, Cone and Sphere support their documented anchors. Use shape.at(target) for the supported shape-to-shape CENTER alignment.
references.limits: Shape-to-shape alignment currently supports CENTER-to-CENTER only. at() is geometric placement/alignment; selecting a support face for a feature is the job of Shape.on().

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Absolute X coordinate in mm, or a target Shape for shape-to-shape alignment.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Absolute Y coordinate in mm. Leave at 0 when x is a target Shape.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Absolute Z coordinate in mm. Leave at 0 when x is a target Shape.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: Datum on this primitive that is placed at the requested coordinate. Defaults to Anchor.CENTER.

parameters.name: child
parameters.description: Child datum for shape-to-shape alignment. Currently only Anchor.CENTER is supported.

references.example:
pin = Cylinder(d=8, h=20, axis=Axis.X).at(10, 0, 5, anchor=Anchor.LEFT)
centered = Sphere(5).at(body)
references.signature: Shape.at(self, x=0, y=0, z=0, *, anchor=<Anchor.CENTER: 'center'>, child=<Anchor.CENTER: 'center'>)

references.name: Shape.on
references.summary: Place a supported within-component feature on a target face.
references.use_when: Put a Hole or another supported feature on an existing Shape and select its entry/support surface with Faces.
references.limits: Shape.on() currently accepts Faces.TOP and Faces.BOTTOM. This is feature placement; component assembly attachment uses Anchor and the component occurrence attach() API.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Existing Shape that receives the feature.

parameters.name: face
parameters.description: Target surface. Currently Faces.TOP or Faces.BOTTOM. Defaults to Faces.TOP.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: In-plane (x, y) offset from the target face centre, in mm. Defaults to (0, 0).

references.name: Shape.attach
references.summary: Anchor a supported feature explicitly to another Shape.
references.use_when: Use this lower-level feature-placement form when parent/child Anchor references are required explicitly.
references.limits: This is legacy within-component feature anchoring. Prefer on() for simple face placement. It is separate from component occurrence attachment used by assemblies.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Existing parent Shape that receives the feature.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Anchor on the target Shape. Defaults to Anchor.TOP.

parameters.name: child
parameters.description: Anchor on the feature being placed. Defaults to Anchor.BOTTOM.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: In-plane (x, y) offset on the parent anchor surface, in mm. Defaults to (0, 0).

references.name: Shape.fillet
references.summary: Round selected solid edges with one radius.
references.use_when: Round one or more edges of a supported feature-based body. Fillet and chamfer use the same edge-selection forms.
references.limits: Edges.VERTICAL and cardinal Box edge selectors require a supported rectangular body. Named profile/vertex selectors require matching Polygon2D ids in a supported extrusion.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Fillet radius in mm.

parameters.name: edges
parameters.description: Edge selection. Use Edges.VERTICAL, a supported two-direction Box edge selector such as FRONT + LEFT, Edges.from_profile(...), Edges.from_vertices(...) or a non-empty sequence of XYZ edge pick points. Defaults to Edges.VERTICAL.

references.name: Shape.chamfer
references.summary: Chamfer selected solid edges by one equal distance.
references.use_when: Bevel one or more edges of a supported feature-based body. Chamfer and fillet use the same edge-selection forms.
references.limits: Edges.VERTICAL and cardinal Box edge selectors require a supported rectangular body. Named profile/vertex selectors require matching Polygon2D ids in a supported extrusion.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Chamfer distance in mm.

parameters.name: edges
parameters.description: Edge selection. Use Edges.VERTICAL, a supported two-direction Box edge selector such as FRONT + LEFT, Edges.from_profile(...), Edges.from_vertices(...) or a non-empty sequence of XYZ edge pick points. Defaults to Edges.VERTICAL.

references.name: Shape.shell
references.summary: Hollow a supported solid and leave selected Faces open.
references.use_when: Create an enclosure-like body with an even wall thickness while removing one or more named planar faces.
references.limits: open= must be one Faces value or a non-empty sequence of Faces values. Support still depends on the underlying feature tree.

parameters.name: thickness
parameters.description: Wall thickness in mm.

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: Face to remove, or a non-empty sequence of Faces values. Defaults to Faces.TOP.

references.name: Shape.fold
references.summary: Fold existing sheet material along one straight line.
references.use_when: Bend material that already exists in a sheet blank. Dimensions and bend allowance come from the sheet's shared rule.
references.limits: This first qualified form supports one straight fold line. The line endpoints and fixed point are fixed finite coordinates.

parameters.name: line
parameters.description: Two XY or XYZ points defining the fold line.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Bend angle in degrees. Defaults to 90.

parameters.name: fixed
parameters.description: Optional XYZ point on the side that must stay fixed.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Native bend-line position: "centerline", "start", "end" or "mould". Defaults to "centerline".

parameters.name: flip
parameters.description: Fold to the opposite side when True. Defaults to False.

references.signature: Shape.fold(self, *, line, angle=90, fixed=None, position='centerline', flip=False)

references.name: Shape.rectangular_pattern
references.summary: Pattern an existing native history feature in one or two directions.
references.use_when: Repeat an already-created native sketch extrusion while keeping one editable SolidCraft rectangular-pattern history feature.
references.limits: The source feature must already be part of this Shape. Supplying a second direction requires both count2 and spacing2.

parameters.name: feature
parameters.description: Existing Sketch.extrude() feature already applied to this Shape, or a non-empty sequence of such features.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of instances in the first direction. Use a positive integer or direct Parameter.

parameters.name: spacing
parameters.description: Instance spacing in the first direction, in mm.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: First pattern direction as Axis.X/Y/Z or a non-zero XYZ vector. Defaults to Axis.X.

parameters.name: count2
parameters.description: Optional instance count for the second direction.

parameters.name: spacing2
parameters.description: Optional spacing for the second direction, in mm.

parameters.name: direction2
parameters.description: Second pattern direction as Axis.X/Y/Z or a non-zero XYZ vector. Defaults to Axis.Y.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: First-direction native alignment: "left", "center" or "right". Defaults to "right".

parameters.name: alignment2
parameters.description: Second-direction native alignment: "left", "center" or "right". Defaults to "right".

parameters.name: reversed
parameters.description: Reverse the first native pattern direction. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: reversed2
parameters.description: Reverse the second native pattern direction. Defaults to False.

references.example: plate.rectangular_pattern(cut, count=3, spacing=24, direction=Axis.X, count2=2, spacing2=28)
references.signature: Shape.rectangular_pattern(self, feature, *, count, spacing, direction=<Axis.X: 'X'>, count2=None, spacing2=None, direction2=<Axis.Y: 'Y'>, alignment='right', alignment2='right', reversed=False, reversed2=False)

references.name: Shape.circular_pattern
references.summary: Pattern an existing native history feature around a fixed axis.
references.use_when: Repeat an already-created native sketch extrusion around an axis while keeping one editable SolidCraft circular-pattern history feature, for example a bolt circle.
references.limits: The source feature must already be part of this Shape. Axis values cover principal or fixed XYZ axes. Native construction-axis, edge-axis and face-axis selectors are not exposed yet.

parameters.name: feature
parameters.description: Existing Sketch.extrude() feature already applied to this Shape, or a non-empty sequence of such features.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Total number of instances including the original. Use a positive integer or direct Parameter.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Rotation axis as Axis.X/Y/Z or a non-zero fixed XYZ direction. Defaults to Axis.Z.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Optional total pattern angle in degrees, as a fixed number or direct Parameter. Omit it for SolidCraft's native 360-degree default.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Optional XYZ point for a shifted fixed axis. With an Axis value and no origin, Forge emits the native principal-axis name directly.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: Native alignment: "left", "center" or "right". Defaults to "right".

parameters.name: reversed
parameters.description: Reverse the native pattern direction. Defaults to False.

references.signature: Shape.circular_pattern(self, feature, *, count, axis=<Axis.Z: 'Z'>, angle=None, origin=None, alignment='right', reversed=False)

references.name: Sketch
references.summary: Create an explicit named 2D sketch scope.
references.use_when: Author one or more 2D profiles before creating a 3D extrusion. A Sketch may be standalone on XY/XZ/YZ or supported by an existing Shape.
references.limits: Sketch(on=target) selects the body modified by the later extrusion. With the default parent=Anchor.TOP, Forge selects the largest +Z planar face at replay time. An explicit plane/origin bypasses face lookup. BOTTOM/CENTER relative placement still requires supported base metadata. offset remains a standalone-plane option. Leave the with-scope before extruding.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Native sketch name. Defaults to "Profile".

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: Optional existing Shape whose surface supports the sketch.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Anchor selecting the supporting surface when on= is used. Defaults to Anchor.TOP.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description: Explicit sketch plane: "XY", "XZ" or "YZ". Defaults to "XY" when on= is not used. With on=, an explicit plane is world-based while on= still selects the body modified by the extrusion.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Optional explicit 3D origin for an explicit plane, in mm. May be used with on= when the Sketch should modify an existing body from a fixed world plane.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Optional signed offset from a standalone origin plane, in mm.

references.example:
with Sketch(name="Base", plane="XY") as sketch:
Rectangle2D(80, 50)
references.signature: Sketch(*, name='Profile', on=None, parent=<Anchor.TOP: 'top'>, plane=None, origin=None, offset=None)

references.name: Sketch.add
references.summary: Add and place a supported 2D profile in this Sketch.
references.use_when: Add a profile explicitly or apply a deliberate sketch-local offset. Dimension-defined profiles default to semantic CENTER. Polygon2D, Text2D and native Slot profiles keep their authored coordinates.
references.limits: Explicit Anchor.CENTER is supported for Circle2D, Rectangle2D and RoundedRectangle2D. Polygon2D, Text2D and native Slot profiles define their own sketch-local coordinates; leave anchor=None for those profile types.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Supported 2D Shape such as Rectangle2D, Circle2D, Polygon2D or a Slot constructor result.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: Optional profile datum. Dimension-defined profiles default to Anchor.CENTER; coordinate-defined profiles keep their own coordinates.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Sketch-local (u, v) displacement in mm. Defaults to (0, 0).

references.name: Sketch.rectangular_pattern
references.summary: Repeat a profile or earlier Sketch result with a native rectangular pattern.
references.use_when: Repeat one Circle, Slot or other supported profile without drawing every copy separately. The returned Sketch result represents the source plus its copies and may be passed to mirror() or another supported Sketch operation.
references.limits: The operation must be authored inside the active Sketch. Current native qualification covers attached Sketch(on=...) use. The two counts may create at most 500 instances in total. Per-instance suppression is not supported. SolidCraft 0.42 stores the curves selected by a mirror when that mirror is created. If a pattern later creates extra curves after its count changes, those new curves are not added to that existing mirror automatically.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: A profile already in this Sketch, or a result returned by rectangular_pattern() or mirror() in the same Sketch.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of instances in the first direction, including the original. Use a whole number from 1 to 500; a dimensionless Parameter may remain editable in SolidCraft.

parameters.name: spacing
parameters.description: Distance between instances in the first direction, in mm. A length Parameter may remain editable in SolidCraft.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: First sketch-local direction: Axis.X, Axis.Y or a fixed non-zero (x, y) vector. Defaults to Axis.X.

parameters.name: count2
parameters.description: Number of instances in the second direction, including the original. Use a whole number from 1 to 500. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: spacing2
parameters.description: Optional distance between instances in the second direction, in mm. When omitted, SolidCraft uses the first spacing.

parameters.name: direction2
parameters.description: Optional second sketch-local direction: Axis.X, Axis.Y or a fixed non-zero (x, y) vector. When omitted, SolidCraft uses the direction perpendicular to the first.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: Position of the original along the first direction: "left", "center" or "right". Defaults to "right".

parameters.name: alignment2
parameters.description: Position of the original along the second direction: "left", "center" or "right". Defaults to "right".

parameters.name: reversed
parameters.description: Reverse placement along the first direction. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: reversed2
parameters.description: Reverse placement along the second direction. Defaults to False.

references.example:
with Sketch(name="Holes", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
circle = Circle2D(d=8)
row = sketch.rectangular_pattern(
circle, count=4, spacing=25, direction=Axis.X
)
with Sketch(name="Slots", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
slot = SlotCenterToCenter2D((0, 0), (20, 0), 8)
pair = sketch.rectangular_pattern(
slot, count=2, spacing=30, direction=Axis.Y
)
references.signature: Sketch.rectangular_pattern(self, source, *, count, spacing, direction=<Axis.X: 'X'>, count2=1, spacing2=None, direction2=None, alignment='right', alignment2='right', reversed=False, reversed2=False)

references.name: Sketch.mirror
references.summary: Mirror a profile or earlier Sketch result over the sketch X or Y axis.
references.use_when: Create symmetric sketch geometry from a Circle, Slot, pattern result or earlier mirror result. The returned Sketch result contains the mirrored copies and may be used by a later supported Sketch operation.
references.limits: The operation must be authored inside the active Sketch. Current native qualification covers attached Sketch(on=...) use. Only the sketch X and Y origin axes are supported. SolidCraft 0.42 stores the curves selected when the mirror is created. If an upstream pattern later creates extra curves after its count changes, those new curves are not added to that existing mirror automatically.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: A profile already in this Sketch, or a result returned by rectangular_pattern() or mirror() in the same Sketch.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Mirror axis. Use Axis.X, Axis.Y, "x" or "y".

references.example:
with Sketch(name="Holes", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
circle = Circle2D(d=8)
sketch.mirror(circle, axis=Axis.Y)
with Sketch(name="Slots", on=board, parent=Anchor.TOP) as sketch:
slot = SlotCenterToCenter2D((0, 0), (20, 0), 8)
pair = sketch.rectangular_pattern(
slot, count=2, spacing=30, direction=Axis.X
)
sketch.mirror(pair, axis=Axis.X)

references.name: Sketch.sheet_metal
references.summary: Create a native sheet-metal body from this closed flat Sketch.
references.use_when: Start a fabricated sheet part from its flat blank before applying holes, folds, hems or other sheet-metal features.
references.limits: The first qualified form requires one standalone XY Sketch with one closed profile. Leave the Sketch scope before creating the sheet.

parameters.name: thickness
parameters.description: Sheet thickness in mm.

parameters.name: bend_radius
parameters.description: Default inside bend radius in mm.

parameters.name: k_factor
parameters.description: Neutral-axis K-factor. Must be greater than 0 and less than 1. Defaults to 0.5.

parameters.name: rule_name
parameters.description: Native SolidCraft sheet-rule name. Defaults to "Forge Sheet".

references.example:

Rectangle2D(80, 40)

bend_radius=2,
k_factor=0.5,
)
references.signature: Sketch.sheet_metal(self, *, thickness, bend_radius, k_factor=0.5, rule_name='Forge Sheet')

references.name: Sketch.extrude
references.summary: Extrude selected profiles from a completed Sketch.
references.use_when: Leave the Sketch context and create or cut material normal to the sketch plane. Use profiles= when the Sketch contains more closed regions than the extrusion should use.
references.limits: A standalone Sketch requires a finite non-zero distance. Depth.THROUGH_ALL is only meaningful for a Sketch attached to an existing Shape and cannot be combined with sym=True. Profile pick points must be fixed finite numbers; Parameters and expressions are not accepted because SolidCraft 0.42 profile points are numeric.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Extrusion distance in mm, or Depth.THROUGH_ALL for an attached Sketch. Positive finite distances follow the plane normal; negative reverses it. THROUGH_ALL cuts through the attached target from the selected support face.

parameters.name: sym
parameters.description: When True, split a positive distance equally across both sides of the sketch plane. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: profiles
parameters.description: Optional non-empty sequence of fixed sketch-local (x, y) points. Each point selects the closed profile containing it. Leave None to extrude every profile.

parameters.name: exact_regions
parameters.description: When True, each profile point selects exactly the SolidCraft region containing that point. Only valid together with profiles=. Defaults to False.

references.name: geometry-constructors
references.summary: Direct 3D primitives and 2D profile constructors.

members.name: Box
members.summary: Create a native rectangular solid around a declared anchor datum.
members.use_when: Model a simple rectangular part directly without introducing a Sketch.
members.limits: The default anchor is CENTER, so an unplaced Box is centred around the model origin in X, Y and Z. Use anchor=BOTTOM for a box whose bottom face centre is at Z=0. Use at() for later placement.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Box size along X, in mm.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Box size along Y, in mm.

parameters.name: thickness
parameters.description: Box size along Z, in mm.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: Box datum placed at model coordinate (0, 0, 0) before later placement. Defaults to Anchor.CENTER.

members.name: Cylinder
members.summary: Create a cylindrical solid centred around the origin by default.
members.use_when: Model a cylinder along Axis.X, Axis.Y or Axis.Z. Use BOTTOM for a Z-axis base, LEFT for an X-axis base or FRONT for a Y-axis base.
members.limits: Anchors refer to world XYZ bounds after choosing the cylinder axis. at() places the selected anchor at the requested coordinate.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Cylinder diameter in mm.

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: Cylinder length along the selected axis, in mm.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Cylinder axis. Use Axis.X, Axis.Y or Axis.Z. Defaults to Axis.Z.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: Cylinder datum placed at model coordinate (0, 0, 0) before later placement. Defaults to Anchor.CENTER.

members.name: Cone
members.summary: Create a native cone or tapered cylinder (frustum).
members.use_when: Model a cone, tapered pin or lightly conical cylinder directly with SolidCraft's native solid.cone feature.
members.limits: Because the two end radii may differ, transverse tangent anchors are intentionally not exposed. Use CENTER or the selected axis' two end anchors: LEFT/RIGHT for X, FRONT/BACK for Y, BOTTOM/TOP for Z.

parameters.name: top_d

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: Length along the selected axis, in mm.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Cone axis. Use Axis.X, Axis.Y or Axis.Z. Defaults to Axis.Z.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: CENTER or one of the two axial end datums.

members.signature: Cone(*, d, top_d=0, h, axis=<Axis.Z: 'Z'>, anchor=<Anchor.CENTER: 'center'>)

members.name: Sphere

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Sphere radius in mm.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: Sphere datum placed at model coordinate (0, 0, 0) before later placement. Defaults to Anchor.CENTER.

members.name: Rectangle2D
members.summary: Create a rectangular 2D profile.
members.use_when: Author a simple rectangle inside an explicit Sketch before extrusion.
members.limits: The dimension-defined profile is centred on the Sketch origin by default. Use Sketch.add(..., offset=(u, v)) for a deliberate local displacement.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Rectangle size along the first local sketch axis, in mm. On XY this is X.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Rectangle size along the second local sketch axis, in mm. On XY this is Y.

members.name: RoundedRectangle2D
members.summary: Create a native rounded-rectangle 2D profile.
members.use_when: A sketch needs a rectangle with true circular corner arcs rather than a polygonal approximation.
members.limits: Current support is inside an explicit Sketch. width and depth must be positive. radius must be positive and below half the shorter side.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Rectangle size along the first local sketch axis, in mm.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Rectangle size along the second local sketch axis, in mm.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Radius of each corner arc, in mm.

members.name: Circle2D
members.summary: Create a circular 2D profile by diameter or radius.
members.use_when: Author a circular profile inside an explicit Sketch.
members.limits: Supply exactly one of d= or r=. The Sketch determines the plane.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Circle diameter in mm. Supply d or r, not both.

parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Circle radius in mm. Supply r or d, not both.

members.name: Polygon2D
members.summary: Create a closed named or unnamed polygon profile.
members.use_when: A 2D profile needs arbitrary straight segments or named vertices and segments that later drive selectors such as Edges.from_profile().
members.limits: At least three 2D points are required. Named and unnamed points cannot be mixed. world=True currently supports only plane="XZ".

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Polygon vertices in order. Use (u, v) pairs, or (name, (u, v)) pairs when naming vertices, in mm.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description: Sketch plane: "XY", "XZ" or "YZ". Defaults to "XY".

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Optional segment names, one per polygon edge in vertex order.

parameters.name: world
parameters.description: When True with plane="XZ", read each input point as world (x, z) instead of native sketch coordinates.

references.name: sketch-slot-constructors
references.summary: Five explicit 2D Slot construction methods mapped directly to SolidCraft sketch.slot.* commands.

members.name: SlotCenterToCenter2D
members.summary: Create a straight Slot from the centres of its two round ends.
members.limits: p0 and p1 must be different points. The straight part runs between these two end centres.

parameters.name: p0
parameters.description: Centre of the first round end as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: p1
parameters.description: Centre of the second round end as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Total Slot width in mm. This is also the diameter of each round end.

members.name: SlotOverall2D
members.summary: Create a straight Slot from its two outermost end points.
members.limits: The distance from p0 to p1 is the total Slot length, including both round ends, and must be larger than width.

parameters.name: p0
parameters.description: Outermost point of the first round end as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: p1
parameters.description: Outermost point of the second round end as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Total Slot width in mm. This is also the diameter of each round end.

members.name: SlotCenterPoint2D
members.summary: Create a straight Slot from its centre and one round-end centre.
members.limits: center and end must differ. The other round-end centre is mirrored through center.

parameters.name: center
parameters.description: Centre of the complete Slot as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Centre of one round end as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Total Slot width in mm. This is also the diameter of each round end.

members.name: SlotArcThreePoint2D
members.summary: Create a curved Slot whose centre arc passes through three points.
members.limits: start, through and end must be three different points.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start point of the Slot centre arc as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: through
parameters.description: A point that the centre arc must pass through, as (x, y) in mm.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End point of the Slot centre arc as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Total Slot width in mm, measured perpendicular to the centre arc.

members.name: SlotArcCenter2D
members.summary: Create a curved Slot from an arc centre and start point.
members.limits: Supply exactly one of end= or sweep=. center and start must differ. sweep must be greater than 0 and less than 360 degrees.

parameters.name: center
parameters.description: Centre of the underlying circular arc as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start point of the Slot centre arc as (x, y) in sketch coordinates, in mm.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Total Slot width in mm, measured perpendicular to the centre arc.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Optional end point of the centre arc as (x, y) in mm.

parameters.name: sweep
parameters.description: Optional positive sweep angle in degrees.

references.name: feature-constructors
references.summary: Mechanical Hole-family and plastic-feature intent added to supported bodies.

members.name: Hole
members.summary: Create a simple cylindrical hole feature.
members.use_when: Make an ordinary drilled hole without a head recess or thread intent.
members.limits: d and finite depth values must be positive. Explicit native Hole features are positioned with at(); face-relative repeated simple holes may also use on() through the existing placement route.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Finished hole diameter in mm.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Hole depth in mm, or Depth.THROUGH_ALL. Defaults to through all.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Optional non-zero XYZ direction vector from the entry point into the material.

members.name: CounterboreHole
members.summary: Create a hole with a cylindrical recess at its entry face.
members.use_when: Seat a cylindrical screw head or other part below the entry surface.
members.limits: counterbore_d must be larger than d. counterbore_depth and finite depth values must be positive. Position this native feature with at().

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Finished main-hole diameter in mm.

parameters.name: counterbore_d
parameters.description: Diameter of the cylindrical recess in mm.

parameters.name: counterbore_depth
parameters.description: Depth of the recess from the entry face in mm.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Main-hole depth in mm, or Depth.THROUGH_ALL. Defaults to through all.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Optional non-zero XYZ direction vector from the entry point into the material.

members.signature: CounterboreHole(*, d, counterbore_d, counterbore_depth, depth=<Depth.THROUGH_ALL: 'through_all'>, direction=None)

members.name: CountersinkHole
members.summary: Create a hole with a conical countersink at its entry face.
members.use_when: Seat a countersunk fastener or specify a hole whose conical entry is part of the hole feature itself.
members.limits: countersink_d must be larger than d. countersink_angle must be between 0 and 180 degrees. Position this native feature with at().

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Finished main-hole diameter in mm.

parameters.name: countersink_d
parameters.description: Diameter of the countersink at the entry face in mm.

parameters.name: countersink_angle
parameters.description: Included countersink angle in degrees. Defaults to 90.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Main-hole depth in mm, or Depth.THROUGH_ALL. Defaults to through all.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Optional non-zero XYZ direction vector from the entry point into the material.

members.signature: CountersinkHole(*, d, countersink_d, countersink_angle=90, depth=<Depth.THROUGH_ALL: 'through_all'>, direction=None)

members.name: ThreadedHole
members.summary: Create a tapped hole with native thread intent.
members.use_when: Preserve tapped-hole manufacturing intent instead of representing the result as an ordinary cylindrical subtraction.
members.limits: The thread designation must be supported by SolidCraft. modeled=True creates actual thread geometry and can be substantially heavier than cosmetic/native thread metadata. Position this native feature with at().

parameters.name: thread
parameters.description: Thread designation such as "M6" or "1/4-20 UNC".

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Drill depth in mm, or Depth.THROUGH_ALL. Defaults to through all.

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Optional explicit tap-drill diameter in mm. When omitted, SolidCraft selects the drill from the thread designation.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Optional non-zero XYZ direction vector from the entry point into the material.

parameters.name: hand
parameters.description: Thread hand, "right" or "left". Defaults to "right".

parameters.name: thread_depth
parameters.description: Optional positive threaded length in mm, independent of drill depth.

parameters.name: modeled
parameters.description: Whether SolidCraft cuts modeled thread geometry. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: ease_out
parameters.description: Optional modeled-thread runout: "standard", "short", or a positive length.

members.signature: ThreadedHole(*, thread, depth=<Depth.THROUGH_ALL: 'through_all'>, d=None, direction=None, hand='right', thread_depth=None, modeled=False, ease_out=None)

references.name: parameters-positioning
references.summary: Keep dimensions symbolic and express readable offsets or parent-bound positions.

members.name: Parameter
members.summary: Represent one named editable CAD dimension.
members.use_when: Keep a value symbolic so generated SolidCraft commands can retain an editable dependency instead of baking in the current Python number.
members.limits: value must be finite. Normal public lower-case model fields are usually promoted to parameters automatically, so explicit Parameter() is mainly useful in lower-level or assembly code.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: SolidCraft parameter name. It must be a valid Python identifier.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Current numeric value of the parameter.

members.name: Placement
members.summary: Absolute pose of one occurrence in its parent coordinate frame.
members.use_when: Declare the pose of a component occurrence at creation or copy time.
members.limits: Placement is occurrence creation state, not a relative move action. Coordinates, rotation axis and angle must evaluate to finite values.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Absolute X position in mm. May be numeric, Parameter or Expression.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Absolute Y position in mm. May be numeric, Parameter or Expression.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Absolute Z position in mm. May be numeric, Parameter or Expression.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Optional (axis, degrees) absolute rotation. axis may be X/Y/Z, Axis, or a non-zero XYZ vector.

members.signature: Placement(x: object = 0, y: object = 0, z: object = 0, rotation: tuple[object, object] | None = None) -> None

members.name: X
members.summary: Axis token with MIN, CENTER and MAX parent-bound placement selectors.
members.use_when: Public X, Y and Z tokens let feature offsets refer to a parent bound, for example X.MIN + 10 or Y.MAX - 10, without hard-coding the current global coordinate.
members.limits: These X/Y/Z tokens are bound selectors, not Axis.X/Y/Z primitive-axis enum values.

members.name: Y
members.summary: Axis token with MIN, CENTER and MAX parent-bound placement selectors.
members.use_when: Public X, Y and Z tokens let feature offsets refer to a parent bound, for example X.MIN + 10 or Y.MAX - 10, without hard-coding the current global coordinate.
members.limits: These X/Y/Z tokens are bound selectors, not Axis.X/Y/Z primitive-axis enum values.

members.name: Z
members.summary: Axis token with MIN, CENTER and MAX parent-bound placement selectors.
members.use_when: Public X, Y and Z tokens let feature offsets refer to a parent bound, for example X.MIN + 10 or Y.MAX - 10, without hard-coding the current global coordinate.
members.limits: These X/Y/Z tokens are bound selectors, not Axis.X/Y/Z primitive-axis enum values.

members.name: up
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the +Z direction.

parameters.name: distance

members.name: down
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the -Z direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Numeric or symbolic CAD distance in mm.

members.name: left
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the -X direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Numeric or symbolic CAD distance in mm.

members.name: right
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the +X direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Numeric or symbolic CAD distance in mm.

members.name: front
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the -Y direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Numeric or symbolic CAD distance in mm.

members.name: back
members.summary: Return a symbolic-safe XYZ offset in the +Y direction.
members.use_when: Express a readable placement offset while preserving Parameter or Expression values.
members.limits: This returns an XYZ tuple; it does not create an Anchor relationship.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Numeric or symbolic CAD distance in mm.

members.name: half
members.summary: Return half of a numeric or symbolic CAD dimension.
members.use_when: Keep midpoint-style arithmetic readable without converting a symbolic CAD dimension to a concrete Python value.
members.limits: Equivalent to value / 2; the input must support that operation.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Numeric, Parameter or Expression value to divide by two.

members.name: midpoint
members.summary: Return the midpoint between two numeric or symbolic dimensions.
members.use_when: Express a centre position while preserving symbolic CAD dependencies.
members.limits: Equivalent to (start + end) / 2; inputs must support symbolic arithmetic.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: First numeric or symbolic coordinate/dimension.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Second numeric or symbolic coordinate/dimension.

members.name: pv
members.summary: Return the concrete Python value of a symbolic CAD dimension.
members.use_when: Python itself genuinely needs a number for validation or control flow.
members.limits: Calling pv() intentionally removes the symbolic dependency at that point. Geometry and placement should normally keep Parameter/Expression objects symbolic so SolidCraft remains editable and associative.

parameters.name: dim
parameters.description: Numeric value, Parameter or Expression to read as a Python float.

members.example:
if pv(clearance) < 0:
raise ValueError("clearance must not be negative")

references.name: attachment-references
references.summary: Use richer local or topology-backed datums when a standard Anchor is not enough.

members.name: AnchorFrame
members.summary: Describe one local attachment point and orientation.
members.use_when: A standard face or corner Anchor is not enough and the mounting datum needs its own local origin plus orientation. A reusable component may expose named AnchorFrame values from anchors(), or an assembly may pass one directly to attach().
members.limits: z and x must be non-zero and must not be parallel. Direct frames on explicitly rotated occurrences have limited support as documented by the assembly guide.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Component-local XYZ attachment point in mm. Defaults to (0, 0, 0).

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Attachment-normal direction as an XYZ vector or Anchor. Defaults to Anchor.UP.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Local X/clocking direction as an XYZ vector or Anchor. Defaults to Anchor.RIGHT.

members.signature: AnchorFrame(origin: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), z: tuple[float, float, float] | scpf.core.Anchor = <Anchor.TOP: 'top'>, x: tuple[float, float, float] | scpf.core.Anchor = <Anchor.RIGHT: 'right'>) -> None

members.name: AnchorTopology
members.summary: Describe an attachment datum that follows native SolidCraft topology.
members.use_when: A relationship should follow a particular edge, adjacent planar face and optionally one endpoint as dimensions change, rather than freezing one XYZ coordinate.
members.limits: edge and on are native selection pick points. Current Forge support focuses on planar-face edges and non-rotated occurrences. z and x, when both supplied, must not be parallel.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: XYZ pick point on the target edge, in component-local mm.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: XYZ pick point on the adjacent planar face, in component-local mm.

parameters.name: corner
parameters.description: Optional XYZ endpoint/corner pick in component-local mm.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Optional non-zero XYZ attachment-normal override.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Optional non-zero XYZ clocking-direction override.

members.signature: AnchorTopology(edge: tuple[float, float, float], on: tuple[float, float, float], corner: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, z: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, x: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None) -> None

references.name: execution-api
references.summary: Lower-level entry points for compiling Shapes or trusted model source files.

members.name: compile_model
members.summary: Compile one Shape tree to a native SolidCraft command document.
members.use_when: Lower-level tooling already has a final Shape object and needs the JSON command plan without executing a model source file.
members.limits: The final value must be a Shape. Normal user workflows usually call the scpf runner/CLI instead.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Final Shape tree to compile.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Model/body name used for generated SolidCraft commands. It must be a valid identifier.

members.name: run_script
members.summary: Execute a trusted SCPF model source file and return its command document.
members.use_when: Programmatic tooling needs the same model-loading/root-selection and compilation behaviour as the SCPF CLI.
members.limits: The source is executed as trusted Python. A file must either end in an explicit root model call or define exactly one unambiguous public model class with build().

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path to the trusted Python model source file.

references.name: diagnostics
references.summary: Public diagnostics for invalid model intent and lost symbolic parameter dependencies.

members.name: ModelError
members.summary: Report unsupported or invalid CAD model intent.
members.use_when: Catch Forge compilation/model validation failures separately from normal Python argument errors when integrating the lower-level compiler API.
members.limits: User model code normally fixes the underlying model instead of handling this exception as a recoverable geometry result.

members.name: ModelParameterWarning
members.summary: Warn that an editable model parameter lost a native CAD dependency.
members.use_when: Tooling wants to detect parameters that became concrete Python values or are only partly associative in the generated SolidCraft model.
members.limits: This is a warning category, not an exception. The preferred fix is to preserve the symbolic relationship or mark an intentional build-time input with a leading underscore.
